core_obligations: Component equivalences (proof lines 7557-7578): h_{-1} = a_X gives (h_{-1})^* : QCoh(O_X) -> QCoh(O_big) an equivalence with quasi-inverse h_{-1,*}, and the same componentwise; QCoh on both total sites is the cartesian modules with quasi-coherent components; since h^* and h_* act componentwise, h^* : QCoh(O_U) -> QCoh(O_{big,total}) is an equivalence with quasi-inverse h_*.

The big-site descent (lines 7580-7593): U is an fppf hypercovering; the simple-descent lemma makes a_{fppf}^* fully faithful with essential image the cartesian modules; by the QCoh characterization the essential image inside QCoh(O_{big,total}) is all of it, so a_{fppf}^* : QCoh(O_big) -> QCoh(O_{big,total}) is an equivalence with quasi-inverse a_{fppf,*}.

Transfer and quasi-inverse (lines 7594-7625): the formal chase through the comparison diagram transfers full faithfulness to a^* on QCoh(O_X) with image in QCoh(O_U) (see notes); conversely for G in QCoh(O_U), h^*G = a_{fppf}^*H with H = a_{fppf,*}h^*G, H = (h_{-1})^*F with F = h_{-1,*}H in QCoh(O_X); going around the diagram h^*G = h^*a^*F and full faithfulness of h^* gives a^*F = G; finally F = h_{-1,*}a_{fppf,*}h^*G = a_*h_*h^*G = a_*G, identifying the quasi-inverse as a_*.
proof_roadmap: Lift the component QCoh equivalences to h^* on the total sites via the componentwise action.
Combine with the big-site simple descent to get the a_{fppf}^* equivalence on QCoh.
Chase the comparison diagram to transfer to a^* and identify the quasi-inverse functorially.
difficulty_reason: Descent theorem (statement 7543-7555, proof 7557-7625): the quasi-coherent module twin of the chapter's sheaf descent theorems - component equivalences lifted through the comparison diagram, the big-site descent restricted to QCoh via the characterization lemma, and the transfer with an explicit functorial identification of the quasi-inverse (F = a_*G computed); the single formal-chase step is recorded in the notes. H2: formal descent bookkeeping over established equivalences.
